rows.cause: google/fonts 93550bd32 (2017-05-09, Marc Foley, #931 "hotfix-titilliumweb: v1.002 added") changed every Titillium binary from fsType 8 to 0. The binaries were edited in place, not re-exported: the FFTM build stamp (2012-09-06) and FFTM source-modified time stay the same, and no glyph-bearing table changed. Every .sfd states FSType: 8. FontForge's exporter writes the stated value (tottf.c: os2->fstype = 0x8; if pfminfo.fstype != -1, the stated value). The original export (googlefontdirectory-hg 52f780bc9, byte-identical to google/fonts 90abd17b4) carries 8, so the converter reproduces FontForge exactly.

rows.cause: fontc 1.0.0 ignores a single-master Glyphs instance's weightClass. glyphs2fontir never sets misc.us_weight_class, so fontbe/os2.rs falls back to 400. Each .sfd's TTFWeight equals the shipped value. tools/workarounds.py (as land.py applies it) writes TTFWeight into the source as FEA, which closes the row. baseline.sh does not apply the workarounds, so the row appears only in the fidelity-only measurement.

rows.cause: ID 6: babelfont's glyphs3 writer maps names.postscript_name (the .sfd FontName) to the Glyphs key postscriptFullName and name ID 20 to postscriptFontName. fontc reads postscriptFontName as name ID 6 and does not use postscriptFullName for the name table, so the stated PS name is lost and fontc derives Family-Style. The prototype patch restores ID 6 = 'Wallpoet'. ID 4 stays 'Wallpoet Regular' because fontc builds it from family plus style (unresolved). The table gate never compares name records (table_gate.py ACCEPTED['name']), and land.py/verify_landed.py do not check PS names. The same loss hits the first batch's CLEAN landings: 24 of 149 styles in families.tsv + families-next.tsv ship a PS name without a style suffix.

proposed_tool_changes.description: Fix the Glyphs 3 name-property mapping. Write names.postscript_name (name ID 6) as `postscriptFontName`, not `postscriptFullName`. Write names.full_name as `postscriptFullName`. Stop writing name ID 20 (the CID findfont name, which has no Glyphs property) as `postscriptFontName`. Map the reader the same way. fontc (glyphs2fontir try_name_id) reads postscriptFontName as name ID 6 and ignores postscriptFullName for the name table, so today an .sfd FontName without a style suffix (Wallpoet, Smythe, NovaCut...) is lost and fontc derives Family-Style. The fix is not FontForge-specific: it affects any conversion to .glyphs.

missed: Contour start point, a converter-fidelity issue in babelfont that the agent did not report. babelfont's model draws closed paths from nodes[0] (shape.rs to_kurbo). Its glyphs3 path conversion (shape.rs:696-735) copies node lists without rotating them. But Glyphs, glyphsLib and fontc treat the LAST node of a closed path as its start (glyphs2fontir toir.rs: 'the starting node of a closed contour is always stored at the end'). So every contour starts one node later than in FontForge's export: Wallpoet 394/394 rotated by 1; Titillium by 1 or 2 in every style (runs/start_point_rotation.txt). Traced on H in TitilliumWeb-Regular: the .sfd starts at (514,0), the .glyphs lists (514,0) first, and the build starts at (514,313). Rendering is unaffected. This explains the agent's unexplained Wallpoet fontspector change (outline_colinear_vectors / outline_short_segments WARN->PASS). The release has 49 FontForge closing duplicates (first point == last), which are not segments. The rotation moves them into the middle of the contour as zero-length segments. My emulation of colinear_vectors.rs gives 61 hits on the release (fontspector: WARN, 61 listed) and 112 on the build; above 100 the check returns PASS early. The 'better' status is therefore an artefact. Fix: rotate closed paths on write and read in the glyphs3 conversion; the same file as the PS-name PR, but a separate change.

The 3442 vs 3441 point count the agent left open: the only glyph that differs beyond the rotation is oslash. The build omits the on-curve (653,380), which is exactly the midpoint of its off-curve neighbours (645,384) and (661,376). The outline is identical (runs/point_counts_wallpoet.txt).
